subject: Mathematics

intro: Lesson 67: Density and pressure. A practical to do at home with an adult nearby. Read it all first.

practical.aim: To find the density of a potato
safety: An adult knows what you are doing and is nearby
Clear a space and tidy up afterwards; wash your hands
method: Weigh the potato on the scales and record its mass in grams
Half fill the jug with water and read the volume in ml
Lower the potato gently into the water until it is just under the surface
Volume of the potato = new reading - first reading (1 ml = 1 cm³)

questions.q: Density 2 g/cm³ and volume 30 cm³. Mass?
Big question: why does a steel ship float but a bolt sink?
questions.a: The ship's total mass is spread over a huge volume including air, so its density is less than water's; the solid bolt is denser than water.

questions.q: A potato has a mass of 220 g and pushes the water up from 500 ml to 700 ml. Find its density.
Will it float in water (density 1 g/cm³)?
questions.a: No: 1.1 g/cm³ is more than water's density, so it sinks
